title: The derived relative tensor product is a two-variable left derived functor
statement:
The derived tensor product $-\otimes^{\mathrm L}_R-$ of [def-sfb-derived-tensor-modules]
(in particular $-\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{\Lambda_X}-$), together with the lax monoidal
structure map of the localization functor, is the left derived functor in two variables
of the relative tensor product of complexes of $R$-modules, with respect to the
quasi-isomorphisms in each variable.

proof.text: Use $\mathcal C$ and the commutative ring object $R$ of [def-sfb-derived-tensor-modules], and put $\mathcal B=\Mod_R(\mathcal C)$. The hypotheses on $\mathcal C$ are exactly those of [lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck], so $\mathcal B$ is Grothendieck abelian. The adjunction and closed symmetric monoidal structure stated in [def-sfb-modobj-internal-hom] apply under these same hypotheses. Thus $\mathcal B$ is closed symmetric monoidal for the relative tensor product $\otimes_R$, not the ambient tensor product of underlying objects.

source.place: only paragraph: application to Mod_R(C); hypotheses from sk-prop-sfb-module-category, clause 3

proof.text: Check additivity of this relative tensor. For $M\in\mathcal B$, the adjunction $T_M=M\otimes_R-\dashv\Hom_R(M,-)$ of [def-sfb-modobj-internal-hom] identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(T_M(0),N)$ with a singleton and $\operatorname{Hom}(T_M(U\oplus V),N)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(U,\Hom_R(M,N))\times\operatorname{Hom}(V,\Hom_R(M,N))$. Consequently $T_M$ preserves the zero object and binary coproducts, with their injections. Zero morphisms factor through the zero object; the biproduct projections are determined by their composites with the injections, so these are preserved too. Applying $T_M$ to $f+g=\nabla\circ(f\oplus g)\circ\Delta$ now gives $T_M(f+g)=T_M(f)+T_M(g)$. Symmetry identifies $-\otimes_R M$ with $M\otimes_R-$, proving additivity in the other variable as well.

source.place: last paragraph: adjunction and closed symmetric monoidal structure; elementary biproduct calculation

proof.text: The ambient category $\mathcal C$ has functorial flat resolutions by the hypotheses in [def-sfb-derived-tensor-modules]. Apply [lem-sfb-modobj-flat-resolutions] with $\mathcal R=R$. Its conclusion supplies functorial flat resolutions in $\mathcal B$ for $\otimes_R$; flatness here means exactness of tensoring over $R$ on either side. This checks the remaining hypothesis of the derived-monoidal theorem without assuming $R$ itself flat in $\mathcal C$.

source.place: statement: inheritance of functorial flat resolutions

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-derived-monoidal] to $\mathcal B$, whose hypotheses were checked in steps 1–3 (a symmetric monoidal structure is braided). It gives a tensor on $D(\mathcal B)$ that is the left derived functor in two variables of the tensor of complexes on $K(\mathcal B)$, for quasi-isomorphisms in each variable, and gives the lax monoidal localization $Q\colon K(\mathcal B)\to D(\mathcal B)$. By [def-sfb-derived-tensor-modules], the tensor in question is precisely $-\otimes_R^{\mathrm L}-$: that definition specifies this very application of the derived-monoidal construction to the relative tensor $\otimes_R$. Its localization structure map is therefore the comparison map belonging to that construction. Hence the asserted derived-functor property concerns the stated functor and its stated comparison map, rather than an independently chosen tensor or lax structure.

source.place: only paragraph: This is part of lem-sfb-derived-monoidal, applied to Mod_R(C) with relative tensor product

proof.text: The parenthetical $R=\Lambda_X$ case is the particular instance already specified in [def-sfb-derived-tensor-modules]. In that instance $D(\mathcal B)=D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$ and the same derived tensor and localization map of step 4 become $-\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{\Lambda_X}-$ and its comparison map. Substitution gives the claimed case without changing the coefficient category.

source.place: last sentence and displayed functor: particular condensed-ring case

proof_origin.place: only paragraph, expanded hypothesis check using sk-prop-sfb-module-category clause 3
